newsitem.title: USA: Small cap stocks post impressive gains.
newsitem.headline: Small cap stocks post impressive gains.

text.p: Small cap stocks surged on Monday with the Russell 2000 and Nasdaq indexes posting impressive runs that, in a rare display, topped the strong gains of the mighty Dow Industrials on a percent basis.

The Russell 2000, a widely-used barometer for tracking small capitalization issues, jumped 2.39 percent to close up 8.45 points at 362.43. The Nasdaq Composite Index was also sharply higher, up 2.60 percent, or 34 points, to 1339.
Adding to strength in the sector, Prudential Securities analyst Claudia Mott turned bullish on small-cap stocks.
"Its a real change of opinion for me to be the least bit positive," she said in a telephone interview.
Speculation about a cut in the capital gains tax on profits from the sale of stocks helped trigger the gains.

"We've got a sellers' strike going on. If you own these stocks, why sell?" said Salomon Brothers' analyst David Shulman. He said it was no coincidence that small caps started surging on Friday afternoon after word came that a budget agreement might be reached in Washington.
On Friday, the Nasdaq rocketed 2.7 percent to 1305. The Russell jumped 2.4 percent to nearly 354.

Mott said the next six months "could be gangbusters" for small caps. She cited their severe underperformance, cheap valuations, the easing of flows out of small cap mutual funds and the possibility of the capital gains tax cut.
Small caps have performed dismally compared with the equity of larger companies over the past year.
For the past 12 months, the Russell 2000 index has fallen "a whopping 20.02 percent -- the second worst trailing 12- month performance in the history of the index," according to Prudential.

Mott, the chief of small cap research, also said attention tends to shift onto the Russell as investors try to guess the changes that will take place when the index is rebalanced at the end of June, as it is every year.
Selling pressure has also abated as the sharp outflow of money out of small cap mutual funds abated recently.
"So many money managers were dealing with redemptions and they've had to sell stock to fund the redemptions," she said.
The Dow Industrials also roared to a record high, up 144 points to 7215. But the index actually trailed the small caps stocks on a percent basis, rising only 2.03 percent.

But both small cap experts were quick to point out that the rally could be short-lived, especially in the face of a possible rise in interest rates. Second quarter earnings performance could also quash a rally.

"More people are ignoring the possibility of a rate hike, and they do so at their peril," said Shulman, Salomon's chief equity strategist. "Because I think we will get a tightening" by the Federal Reserve sometime this year.

In a report released ahead of the run-up in small cap stocks in the past two sessions, Dean Witter's chief investment strategist Peter Canelo said a sustainable recovering might be "in the offing" for small caps if the Fed raises rates only once or twice more.

"But should the Fed push rates...more than 50 basis points from current levels, even a capital gains tax rate cut might do little more than provide a temporary reprieve in the ongoing bear market in smaller capitalization issues," Canelo said in the report.
The Russell 2000's gains were the second- and third-largest daily advances since the index's inception in January 1987, according to the Frank Russell company.

Among the 33 companies Mott said are quantitatively attractive were Arvin Industries Inc, Aviall Inc, Cyrix Corp, Arthur J. Gallagher & Co, Hutchinson Technology Inc, IHOP Corp, Innovex Inc, New England Business Service Inc, Standard Products Co, Techne Corp, Wall Data Inc and Zebra Technologies.
